children: Mid- and smallcap valuations may be above their historical averages, but the premium is not necessarily difficult to justify if earnings growth remains strong, said Naveen Kulkarni, CIO - PMS and Listed Equity Alternates at Axis AMC. Speaking on the sidelines of Moneycontrol’s Mutual Fund Summit - Delhi edition, Kulkarni said investors should focus on the growth potential of businesses rather than assess valuations in isolation.

“Multiples have to be justified by growth,” Kulkarni said, adding that the broader macroeconomic environment remains supportive of earnings expansion. He added that midcaps and smallcaps are trading at elevated valuation levels, but argued that the longer-term compounding potential of businesses needs to be considered alongside these multiples.
Midcaps trade one standard deviation above mean

According to Kulkarni, midcap valuations are currently around one standard deviation above their normal levels, while smallcaps are trading at approximately 1.3-1.4 standard deviations above the mean.
“It's not extremely expensive, but let's say it's expensive,” he said, while adding that the valuation premium could be supported by growth prospects.

Kulkarni also pointed out that one-year forward earnings multiples for mid- and smallcap indices need to be assessed carefully, given the limited analyst coverage of a large part of the universe and the difficulty in establishing reliable consensus earnings estimates.
“Multiples are not necessarily very, very logical, especially when we are looking at one-year forward earnings,” he said.

The need for selective stock-picking was emphasised, even as opportunities in the broader market remain. “One can be a little more judicious in terms of picking, but I think there's still a lot of money to be made there,” Kulkarni said.
Earnings recovery could support broader market valuations

Kulkarni's comments come against the backdrop of a stronger-than-expected June quarter earnings performance, where midcaps saw 23 percent earnings growth while smallcaps outperformed with 31 percent earnings growth. Meanwhile, largecaps trailed with 21 percent earnings growth.
The earnings recovery helped strengthen investor confidence in the broader market, with both midcap and smallcap segments witnessing consecutive buying for 5 months.

The broader earnings outlook remains linked to the ability of companies to sustain growth through the rest of FY27. Kulkarni said that a supportive macroeconomic environment and improving nominal growth could provide a foundation for the smaller-company segment, although the earnings trajectory will need to validate the valuations being assigned to these stocks.
Growth is attracting capital to the broader market
Kulkarni said investor flows tend to move towards segments where earnings growth becomes scarce or more attractive.
“Whatever becomes scarce, that's what attracts flows,” he said.

He noted that Nifty earnings growth had remained relatively subdued over the previous two financial years, at around 2-3 percent in FY25 and 6-7 percent in FY26. Against this backdrop, smaller companies could benefit disproportionately from a pickup in nominal economic growth, given their ability to adjust more quickly to changing business conditions.
“Smaller companies tend to be more nimble,” Kulkarni said, explaining that these businesses can respond to changes in the operating environment and benefit when growth momentum improves.

This growth-seeking behaviour is not limited to India. Kulkarni pointed to emerging markets, where investors have been attracted to companies delivering strong earnings growth, including major chipmakers and technology businesses.

title: Mid, smallcaps still offer opportunities despite premium valuations: Naveen Kulkarni of Axis AMC
